# Modern Financial Technology (MFT)

> MFT is a CPA-led firm that implements Odoo ERP, runs internal audit and acts as your Virtual CFO: one team, one set of numbers, in Egypt, Saudi Arabia and the US.

## Services
- [Odoo ERP Implementation](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/services/odoo-erp/): Odoo ERP implementation by MFT is a finance-led deployment: certified Odoo partners who are also licensed accountants configure the system around your chart of accounts, tax obligations and controls, so the ledger is right from day one.
- [Internal Audit](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/services/internal-audit/): Internal audit by MFT is a risk-based programme run by a CPA-led team inside your ERP: controls are tested, findings are ranked by financial impact, and each one carries an owner, a fix and a deadline.
- [Virtual CFO](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/services/virtual-cfo/): Virtual CFO by MFT is a monthly finance-leadership service: an MFT accountant delivers a management pack, a cash-flow forecast and a decision review, with the Virtual CFO agent doing the analysis from your ERP.
- [Financial Consulting](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/services/financial-consulting/): Financial consulting by MFT is project-based advisory for one-off decisions such as feasibility, restructuring, valuation, cross-border structuring and tax, grounded in your actual ledger.
- [Business Analysis](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/services/business-analysis/): Business analysis by MFT documents how orders, stock, production and cash actually move through your company and specifies what a system must do about it, before anything is configured.
- [User Training](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/services/training/): User training by MFT is role-based Odoo and finance training delivered on your own configuration and data, in Arabic or English, with recorded sessions and bilingual guides.
- [Technical Support](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/services/technical-support/): Technical support by MFT is an Odoo administration and maintenance agreement with agreed response times: user issues, report changes, access rights, upgrades and integrations, handled by people who know your chart of accounts.
- [Claude for teams: implementation and training](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/services/claude-team/): Claude for teams with MFT is a service that sets up Claude Team for your company (members, permissions, single sign-on, projects, connections to work tools) and trains each team to use it under a written data policy. MFT is independent and not part of Anthropic.

## MFT Intelligence AI agents
- MFT Intelligence is a managed AI-agent service from Modern Financial Technology: MFT runs specialised audit, CFO and finance-operations agents on a client’s ERP data and delivers reviewed findings, draft entries and reports under a governance policy enforced in code.
- Auditor agent (Available now): Continuous review of your books against ISA 320 materiality thresholds calibrated to your business. Problems surface when they happen, not at the annual audit, and the risk of a material misstatement drops.
- Virtual CFO agent (Available now): Profitability, cash flow and budget-variance analysis every month. CFO-level visibility without the cost of a full-time hire, built for small and mid-sized companies.
- Accountant agent (Internal validation, launching soon): Complete month-end close checklist. A faster, more accurate monthly close with your team keeping the final say.
- Warehouse, inventory & production agent (Internal validation, launching soon): Stock levels, reorder points, valuation and slow-moving items. Less capital locked in idle stock; receiving and production discrepancies caught early.
- HR agent (Internal validation, launching soon): Headcount, probation periods and contracts approaching expiry. Payroll discrepancies surface early and no contract renewal is forgotten.
- Payroll & workforce-cost agent (Internal validation, launching soon): Workforce cost by department and project. You see where labour cost is going before the payroll run closes.
- Sales & CRM agent (Internal validation, launching soon): Pipeline, conversion and customer concentration. Margin and credit exposure become visible per customer, not just per month.
- Procurement agent (Internal validation, launching soon): Purchase-order to receipt to invoice matching. Leakage in the purchase cycle is caught at the order, not at the audit.
- Tax & compliance agent (Internal validation, launching soon): VAT and withholding checks per country (Egypt 14%, Saudi 15%). Tax exposure is known before the return, not after the assessment.
- Treasury & cash-flow agent (Internal validation, launching soon): 13-week cash-flow view from open receivables, payables and commitments. No cash surprise reaches the board first.
- Fixed assets agent (Internal validation, launching soon): Register completeness against purchases. The asset register matches reality and the depreciation charge is defensible.
- Project costing agent (Internal validation, launching soon): Cost-to-complete and margin per project. Project margin is known during the project, not at handover.
- Pricing: No fixed prices are published. Each engagement is priced to entity count, transaction volume and reporting scope. Request a quote: https://www.seg-audit.com/en/request-quote/

## Where we work
- [Egypt](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/egypt/): MFT is a CPA-led financial technology and audit firm headquartered in Korba, Heliopolis, Cairo, serving companies across Egypt with Odoo ERP implementation, internal audit and Virtual CFO reporting, in Arabic and English.
- [Saudi Arabia](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/saudi-arabia/): MFT serves Saudi companies with ZATCA phase-two compliant Odoo ERP implementation, internal audit programmes and Virtual CFO reporting, delivered on site and remotely in Arabic and English, with client data remaining on the client’s own systems in line with the Saudi Personal Data Protection Law.

## Insights (blog)
- [Materiality is a method, not a round number](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/materiality-isa-320-threshold/): Under ISA 320, materiality is the size of misstatement that could reasonably influence the decisions of people who read the financial statements. It is set by choosing a benchmark that reflects how the business is judged, such as profit before tax or revenue, applying a percentage that reflects its risk, and setting a lower performance materiality beneath it.
- [ZATCA phase two inside Odoo: what must be right before go-live](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/zatca-phase-two-odoo-checklist/): Before going live with ZATCA phase two in Odoo, confirm that entity and branch details match the ZATCA portal, the EGS unit is onboarded with a production CSID, standard invoices clear and simplified invoices report within 24 hours, mandatory invoice fields and credit note references are correct, and every invoice type passes the ZATCA sandbox.
- [Egyptian e-invoicing in Odoo: seven configuration mistakes that block submissions](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/egypt-eta-einvoicing-odoo-mistakes/): Most Egyptian Tax Authority e-invoice rejections from Odoo come from master data, not tax: products without an approved item code, customers with the wrong identification type, branch addresses that differ from the registration, unlisted units of measure, discounts at the wrong level, missing exchange rates, and credit notes without the original document’s UUID.
- [The eleven months your annual audit does not see](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/continuous-audit-eleven-months/): Continuous internal audit reviews the whole population of transactions throughout the year instead of a sample once a year. It surfaces issues the annual audit is not designed to catch in time, such as duplicate payments, near-duplicate vendors, approvals outside the matrix and cut-off errors, and it shortens the external audit by leaving a ready evidence trail.
- [Agents draft. People approve. Why we built it that way.](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/agents-draft-people-approve/): In MFT Intelligence, AI agents never post to the ledger. They draft correcting entries and adjustments with the evidence attached, and named, registered people approve them by materiality tier: one approver below the ISA 320 threshold, a second at or above it. Corrections are made by reversing entries, never deletions, and every step is logged.
- [Preparing Egypt’s monthly VAT return from Odoo, without the spreadsheet](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/egypt-vat-return-odoo/): Prepare it from Odoo’s tax report, not a spreadsheet. Map every tax in use to the correct tax grid, reconcile output and input VAT on the report to the VAT accounts in the general ledger, compare sales and purchases with the e-invoices accepted on the ETA portal, then file by the statutory deadline and set the tax lock date.
- [Egypt’s e-receipt system: what changes for retail, and what Odoo POS needs](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/egypt-e-receipt-b2c/): Egypt’s e-receipt system requires businesses selling to consumers to issue each receipt electronically and transmit it to the Egyptian Tax Authority, with a unique identifier and a QR code. Unlike B2B e-invoicing, it runs at the point of sale in high volumes, so every POS terminal must be registered and integrated, and receipts reconciled to the ledger daily.
- [Zakat or corporate income tax in Saudi Arabia: who pays which, and what the ledger must show](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/zakat-vs-corporate-income-tax-saudi/): In Saudi Arabia, the share of a company owned by Saudi and GCC nationals is generally subject to Zakat, at 2.5% of the zakat base, while the share owned by non-Saudi shareholders is subject to corporate income tax, at a standard 20% of taxable profit. Companies with mixed ownership pay both, split by ownership.
- [The phases of an Odoo accounting implementation, and the mistakes that cost the most](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/odoo-accounting-implementation-steps/): A sound Odoo accounting implementation runs in phases: design the chart of accounts, configure taxes and journals, set access rights and approvals, load and reconcile opening balances, run Odoo in parallel with the old system for at least one closed period, then go live with lock dates set. Skipping the parallel run is the costliest mistake.
- [FIFO or average cost in Odoo: choosing a valuation method you can live with](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/odoo-inventory-valuation-fifo-avco/): Choose FIFO when purchase costs move and you need cost of goods sold to reflect the actual layers consumed; choose average cost (AVCO) when items are interchangeable and you want smoother margins. In Odoo, set the method and automated valuation on the product category before transactions begin, because changing it mid-year revalues stock and breaks comparability.
- [A month-end close checklist for Odoo that a reviewer can sign](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/month-end-close-checklist-odoo/): A month-end close in Odoo should reconcile every bank and cash journal, review receivable and payable ageing, post accruals and deferrals, reconcile inventory valuation to the ledger, post depreciation, reconcile VAT, review the trial balance and management accounts, and only then set the lock date, so the closed period cannot change without a logged decision.
- [What is internal audit, and what does a mid-sized company actually get from it?](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/what-is-internal-audit/): Internal audit is an independent, objective function that tests whether a company’s risk management, controls and governance actually work, and reports findings and recommendations to the board or owners. Unlike an external audit, which gives an opinion on the annual financial statements for outside users, internal audit works for the organisation throughout the year and looks forward.
- [Segregation of duties in Odoo: who should never hold both keys](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/segregation-of-duties-odoo/): Segregation of duties means no single person controls every stage of a transaction: authorising it, recording it, holding the asset and reconciling the result. In Odoo it is enforced by assigning users to access groups that separate incompatible tasks and by adding approval steps. Where the team is too small, independent review of changes and reconciliations compensates.
- [Three-way match: the purchase control that stops paying for what never arrived](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/three-way-match-purchase-controls/): A three-way match compares the purchase order, the goods receipt and the vendor bill before a payment is approved. Quantities and prices on the bill must agree with what was ordered and what was actually received, within agreed tolerances. Differences are held for review instead of being paid, so the company pays only for goods it ordered and received.
- [Bank reconciliation is a control, not a chore](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/bank-reconciliation-controls/): A bank reconciliation is a control because it proves that every movement on the bank statement is recorded in the ledger and every recorded payment actually went through the bank. To work as a control it is done at least monthly, with reconciling items explained and aged, no unexplained difference carried forward, and review by someone who makes no payments.
- [Virtual CFO or full-time CFO: how to tell which one you need](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/virtual-cfo-vs-full-time-cfo/): A Virtual CFO makes sense when a company needs senior finance judgement on planning, cash, reporting and controls, but not every day, typically a growing or owner-managed business with a bookkeeper or small team. A full-time CFO is the better choice when significant finance decisions arise daily, the team needs an on-site leader, or investors and lenders expect one.
- [How to build a 13-week cash flow forecast from your ledger](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/thirteen-week-cash-flow-forecast/): A 13-week cash flow forecast projects cash receipts and payments week by week for the next quarter using the direct method. It starts from the reconciled bank balance, builds receipts from open receivables and expected sales, and payments from payables, payroll, tax and debt service. It is rolled forward every week and compared with actual results.
- [Odoo 20 for finance teams: what changes, what to ignore, what to test](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/odoo-20-whats-new-for-finance-teams/): According to the Odoo 20 release notes, the finance changes that matter are in the bank and payables: bank entries must originate from bank transactions, bills can be paid through bank payment initiation where bank and country allow, and duplicate bills get red or yellow warnings. An AI assistant follows. Re-test ETA and ZATCA e-invoicing after upgrading.
- [Odoo 20 AI agents in finance: useful, billable, and in need of an approver](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/odoo-20-ai-agents-finance-controls/): According to the Odoo 20 release notes, AI agents are Enterprise-only records with instructions, skills, knowledge sources and triggers. They can create and update records, run in automated and scheduled actions, and every run is logged. Each request consumes IAP credits. Govern them like a new team member: the agent drafts, a named person approves.
- [Odoo 20 bank reconciliation and bill payments: the new rules and the controls they need](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/odoo-20-bank-reconciliation-and-bill-payments/): According to the Odoo 20 release notes, every journal entry affecting a bank account must originate from a bank transaction, a summary report shows reconciled and unreconciled items at period end, and bills can be paid through payment initiation where bank and country allow. Pair these with approval before payment, few payment initiators and a reviewed duplicate queue.
- [Should you upgrade to Odoo 20? A plan for companies on 17, 18 and 19](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/odoo-20-upgrade-plan-17-18-19/): It depends on your current version. On Odoo 17, standard support was planned to end in September 2026, so plan the upgrade now. On 18, upgrade within the next twelve months. On 19, upgrade when a specific Odoo 20 feature pays for itself. Whatever the timing, test the ledger, taxes and e-invoicing before go-live.
- [Odoo 20 inventory valuation changes: what they mean for COGS and margin](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/odoo-20-inventory-valuation-changes/): According to the Odoo 20 release notes, valuation accruals can post directly to the inventory valuation account, COGS updates retroactively when a cost changes after delivery, landed costs can target individual products, and inventory can be reported at a past date. Margins become more accurate, so cost changes and period locks need tighter control.
- [AI in accounting: a practical 2026 guide for finance teams](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/ai-in-accounting-guide-2026/): AI in accounting is the use of machine learning and language models to draft, match, classify and test accounting records: suggesting bill lines, matching bank transactions, flagging duplicates and scoring every transaction for risk. It speeds preparation and widens review coverage, but a named person must still approve what it drafts, and every output must trace to source records.
- [AI for journal entries and bank reconciliation: automate it safely](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/ai-journal-entries-bank-reconciliation/): AI automates journal entries and bank reconciliation by predicting how documents should be coded, matching bank transactions to open invoices, bills and payments, and drafting entries for review. It should handle high-volume, well-evidenced items such as customer receipts and bank charges, while a named person approves judgemental entries, owns matching tolerances and reviews every unmatched or written-off difference.
- [AI financial fraud detection: red flags, models and limits](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/ai-financial-fraud-detection/): AI financial fraud detection scores every transaction in the ledger against red-flag patterns, such as duplicate payments, near-duplicate vendors, approvals outside the matrix and round manual entries posted late at month-end, and routes the highest scores to a person. A flag is a lead to investigate with evidence, never proof of fraud or of a misstatement.
- [AI in the month-end close and financial reporting: what to automate](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/ai-month-end-close-financial-reporting/): AI helps the month-end close by doing the matching, reconciling, variance scanning and first-draft commentary that consume most of the close calendar, and by testing every entry before the period is locked. It should draft accruals, adjustments and explanations for a named person to approve, never post them, and every reported number must trace to cited records.
- [Continuous auditing with AI vs traditional audit: side by side](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/continuous-auditing-ai-vs-traditional-audit/): Continuous auditing with AI tests every transaction against defined rules shortly after it is posted, instead of testing a sample of a closed period months later. It shortens the time between an error and its detection and extends coverage to the whole population. It does not replace the external auditor’s opinion, professional judgement, or a named approver for each finding.
- [Full-population testing with AI vs audit sampling: a practical guide](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/full-population-testing-ai-vs-sampling/): Full-population testing with AI means running an audit procedure on every transaction in a defined population instead of a statistical or judgemental sample. It removes sampling risk for the attributes tested, but it does not remove the need to prove the data is complete, design the right tests, and have a person evaluate each exception against evidence.
- [AI and segregation of duties: internal controls when agents are users](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/ai-segregation-of-duties-internal-controls/): AI changes segregation of duties because an AI agent that can create or update accounting records is, for control purposes, a user. It must sit in the SoD matrix with a role, an owner and minimum rights. Keep its output in draft for a named person to approve, and use AI to test conflicts across every transaction.
- [AI audit trail and zero hallucination: the evidence-or-silence rule](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/ai-audit-trail-zero-hallucination/): An AI audit trail links every AI output to the specific records it retrieved, the instruction and run that produced it, and the person who reviewed it. Zero hallucination is enforced, not hoped for: under the evidence-or-silence rule, a finding that cites no record, or a number absent from its cited records, is rejected.
- [Odoo 20 AI features for accounting: a feature-by-feature map](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/odoo-20-ai-features-accounting/): Odoo 20’s AI features for accounting are AI-powered financial insights, agents that create and update records inside automated and scheduled actions, a database connection through MCP, and automatic model selection, all billed per request through IAP credits. Bill line prediction and duplicate detection sit beside them. Each needs an owner, scoped access rights and a named approver.
- [Connecting AI to Odoo for continuous auditing: access, evidence and approvals](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/connect-ai-to-odoo-continuous-audit/): To connect AI to Odoo for continuous auditing, give the analysis layer its own dedicated user with read access only, through the external API or the MCP connection listed in Odoo’s 20 release notes. Keep client data on the client’s system, make every finding cite the record ids it read, and route any proposed correction to a named approver.
- [Odoo 20 purchase approvals: automate the matrix, keep the control](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/odoo-20-purchase-approvals-automation/): To automate purchase approvals in Odoo 20, write the approval matrix first, then map each row to a mechanism: the Purchase Order Approval setting for order thresholds, the Approvals app for categories and several approvers, and automation rules with activity plans for vendor changes. Let AI agents draft records only, and test every month for split orders and bypasses.
- [AI accounting on Odoo 20, step by step: a 90-day rollout with gates](https://www.seg-audit.com/en/blog/odoo-20-ai-accounting-step-by-step/): To apply AI accounting on Odoo 20, roll it out in three 30-day phases with a gate between each: first assistive features such as bill line prediction and financial insights, then AI in bank reconciliation, then agents that draft entries for approval. Each gate requires measured error rates, named approvers and retained evidence before the next phase starts.

## Facts
- CPA-led team; Odoo Certified Partner; ISO-aligned internal controls; 500+ reports delivered; Egypt, Saudi Arabia, US.
- Agents draft only; every action needs a named human approval (two above ISA 320 materiality); corrections by reversal, never deletion.
- AI governance policy enforced in code; run log retained 7 years (ISA 230); client data stays on the client’s own ERP.
